$schema: host.user — runtime shape captured 2026-05-13 from a real Cloud Portal iframe. Returns an Auth0-style claims object (JWT-claim namespacing). Values redacted to placeholders; structure preserved verbatim. NOTE — this query was NOT documented in `application.context`'s declared type; the user identity requires a SEPARATE `client.query('host.user')` call.
name: <First Last>

user_identity_key.decision: Use `host.user.sub` (Auth0 subject claim) as the stable user identifier when one is needed. Format: `auth0|<id>`.
user_identity_key.rationale: It is the stable JWT subject claim. `email` is a stronger human-readable identifier but can change (email rename, account merge). For PRD-000 (tenant-only entitlement per ADR-0011) `sub` is accepted by the EntitlementStore signature but NOT consulted. PRD-002 may use it for seat assignment.

user_display_name_chain.decision: For the post-gate welcome screen heading: prefer `host.user.given_name` first (just 'Welcome, Christian'), fall back to `host.user.name` (full name), fall back to `host.user.email.split('@')[0]`, fall back to the literal 'there'.
user_display_name_chain.rationale: Real-tenant capture showed `given_name: 'Christian'` and `name: 'Christian Hahn'`. The welcome template `'Welcome, {name}'` reads more naturally with the given_name only (per UI spec § 3.4 + POC `state-allowed.html`). `name` is a documented fallback if `given_name` is unavailable (older accounts).

auth0_claims_namespace.note: The `https://auth.sitecorecloud.io/claims/*` keys are Auth0 namespaced custom claims. Use them ONLY if you need the JWT-level org/tenant context BEYOND what `application.context` already provides — for the paywall pattern, `application.context.marketplaceAppTenantId` is sufficient. Adopters writing per-feature server-side guards (PRD-001 `withEntitlement` HOF) may want to verify these claims directly against the Auth0 issuer.
